He he. So, the reactor... You really want to know? Well, then. Let's see. It's kind of your fault, you know. You don't agree?

I'll explain. Or rather, I'll quote Turischev:

"Okay, we're done with the goblins, and now there's no one to fix the reactor which we need to destroy in order to stop the Eclipse. It’s just that I’m afraid - Catherina's reactor is quite unusual! Do you really think the Queen needs Firebird to cure the Blight? Well, for that, too. But mostly as an energy source. The core of the reactor. If we manage to destroy the reactor and let the Firebird out, an ocean of energy will be released! I think the gift Klavdia gave you could probably be useful in a situation like this.

And there's another thing... During the fight, the goblins kept yelling something about a demon. Can Catherina control demons now? It's a terrifying thought - imagine what she might be capable of..."

Do you understand now? You gave Catherina the ability to reach the deeper layers of the Astral! But it's not that simple...

Yes, they were yelling about a demon for a reason. The reactor itself was the "demon" connected to the energy systems of the ship. So this combination of the demon and Firebird led to unexpected results and incredible efficiency.

It's hard to describe that battle. I can say that you defeated the creature, but only just. And the Firebird helped... But is it enough to paint a picture of what happened? I hope you'll see it yourself some day.

But what did you do after the victory? Toss a coin... and see Skrakan in his physical form...

"Oh! I thought ghosts couldn't feel a thing... no heat, no pain. But I'm definitely feeling both. Am I alive?

Oh wait! I remember you! You released my spirit from under Tep’s control, and I told you the truth about the cataclysm!

So now I'm alive? I came back to life? It's not possible! I have to be dead! Do you understand? Dead! My mistake caused so many deaths. They’re all dead, but I'm alive. This... This is painful. Why did you bring me back? I made so many mistakes. Why do you need me, a failure who died because of his foolishness?

The deeper the Astral, the easier it is to affect it. But you are not strong enough to create life from astral matter on your own. Not even Great Mages can do that. It's something only divine power, or something close to it, can accomplish. So someone helped you bring the old fool back to this wonderful world. And there is a reason for it, I imagine? Tell me more before I turn to ashes again. Hurry.

Oh, Catherina, Catherina... Your pride will be your undoing! No, I don't think she made this decision on her own. Breaking a Seal! It's unthinkable! Nobody can survive it, and Catherina is not suicidal. And she’s rather weak-willed, so I’m sure there is someone behind this.

You absolutely can't kill Catherina! Don’t even think about it! Killing a Great Mage near a Seal will break it for sure, and we will all be doomed. We need to neutralize her somehow before she does something we can't undo...

At any rate, it's time to act. There's no point in guessing. We have to stop her. Let's go!"

Harat was consumed by power which turned him into an Elemental of fire and darkness.

"So Catherina managed to capture not one but two dragons! I heard the rumors but didn't quite believe them. Who could have known...

There is no time to dwell on how she did it. Our enemy has a powerful weapon in their hands. The power of the dragons! And now the world is in great danger.

Hold on to your weapons - this will be a difficult battle!" warned Anton Turischev.

Harat didn't hide his elation:

"The pain... The pleasure... The power! I am even stronger than dragons. I will destroy the Seal and free Sarn! Witness the greatest sorcery in the history of Sarnaut... The ultimate sorcery!

May the ritual begin!"

That battle was indescribable. In addition to battling Harat, you had to keep an eye on Catherina so she wouldn't open the Seal.

"You will never defeat me... I will never die... And you will never resurrect! You could hardly defeat my shadow! What do you hope to accomplish?! Even my shadow nearly killed you. Why do you keep fighting? You're doomed! Why prolong your suffering? Are you trying to interfere with the Queen's plans?

I'm... fading... It doesn't matter. This ship is an arrow fired at the heart of the world. And it reached its target! The ritual... can't... be stopped..." Even though Harat was defeated, the world was still on the brink of destruction.

Sarn joined the battle again. He kept trying to break free.

"Why did you betray me? I could have created a new, more beautiful world for you. But you chose death... So be it! What wonderful, fierce people I created! Go on, attack me! It will only make me stronger! I used to give gifts to people. Now I only have curses! This pathetic Seal can't hold me! Die! Perish! Cease to exist! Freedom is so close!

You are my best creation. The best destroyers in all the worlds! You have fulfilled your purpose. This. Is. The end.

So the battle began on the surface of one of the Seals. Sarn did everything he could to destroy it, but... this attempt to break free was unsuccessful. He was defeated once again:

"What did I create...? What has become of you...? How could you... surpass... me?"

You are going to defeat an enemy. The Architect's Archonts.

Who are the Archonts?

The Architects are creatures with one shared consciousness - basically it's the Architect, but for functional purposes he splits himself into parts with different tasks. The most important ones, sort of like commanders, were the Archonts. You've already met those Archonts on Dane... In the Fractal, there will be a few familiar faces among the enemies.

You have already destroyed one of the Archonts - Aine, the Archont of Time. He had very useful abilities: he controlled time, travelled to the past, changed events. Unfortunately for him, this ability of his was transferred to you, and you were able to use it to avoid a series of defeats.

Unfortunately, once Aine was destroyed, you lost this ability...

Let's get back to the one who tasked you with defeating this enemy. Izbor Yavorsky!

"Look into the faces of our warriors. What do you see in their eyes? Anger and hope! They are willing to fight and die to win. And the banner that flew over the enemy citadel only strengthened their faith and will.

Our Alliance... I must admit, it turned out to be successful. And it's good that the two heroes who went with you were Danes - the Imperials won't be able to say that someone's contribution to the victory was more significant.

Although it’s too early to talk about victory - we're counting chickens before they hatch. The remaining forces are scattered all over the allod, the traitor fled - but we have other problems now! We still need to seal this accursed Path so that no creature can get here. And in this Fractal, the way Eladia called it, we're going to face a lot of trouble.

But there's no other way! Let's move!"

Dane was saved, and you closed another breach. But listen to what Eladia had to say:

"So, this is the end of the Path. But is the war over? The Architect was defeated, but he wasn't destroyed. And these things keep happening - we deal with one threat, and another pops up, then another. Chaos, Order, Architects, Demons, fanatics - what are we supposed to do with all that?

Praise the heroes, remember the fallen... And then we do it all over again. War after war, catastrophe after catastrophe. Sometimes I think Order wouldn't be so bad after all. It's all a vicious circle. And I will do my best to break it!"

So, the Archont of War, Kreeg. As you remember, your paths crossed on the Kurbatskoe field. Kreeg is the commander who led the invasion of Dyne, and I think many residents of this allod have a scored to settle with him.

You already defeated him once, but he survived. Damaged but not defeated, he will try to stop your invasion of the Fractal.

“What, you can’t wait to die? That's what toying with the Threads does to you.

Now that we're finished with the weaklings.. we will face the incredibly powerful Architects who have just made us their primary target.

What do we do? We knock on their door, of course," said Eladia.

Do I need to tell you that he's going to fail?

I'll quote Eladia:

"Implements of war should be buried in the deepest abysm. The Astral will devour what's left of this Archont. Demons will tear it apart. Among all the creations of Sarn, they must hate the Architects more than anyone.

It's ironic!"

The Archont whose goal was to make your world part of the Architect's reality...

"So he has broken into our world. Who is he? I have no idea. But the Archonts clearly needed him for some reason. Don't give me this look - I know about as much as you do!

Whoever he is, we need to close the Path to stop them from invading. If we fail, everything we've done so far will be for nothing."

It was the Archont whose goal was to create a new Path that would finally connect the world of the Architects with Sarnaut. He also failed and died before he could exit the portal.

You didn’t have a chance to meet the next enemy in battle. However, he carefully watched all your actions. Zenith, the Archont Observer, is a scout who allows the Architect to carefully assess the situation and react accordingly.

Now he is hiding at the very top of his citadel. Catherina will help you deal with him. That's why she brought the Eclipse here.

This is what Eladia said about it:

"Hah! That's one sturdy structure. The cannons of the Eclipse could fire at this fortress for years with no result. The Architects might get a little uncomfortable, but that's it.

Anyway, I helped you get the Eclipse here, and now it will provide support in battle. I guess we need to reach the top of that tower, right?"

The Eclipse helped you defeat this Archont... But another familiar face was waiting for you up ahead.

So you're standing in front of that portal. The probability of a new invasion is significant... And you have already seen what happens when the Architects try to influence the living flesh of your world. Modificants, all this madness is what the Architects' influence brings.

You are lucky that the Sculptor has been separated from the Unity for so long. Or the Ascension and Transmutation would have been inevitable.

I'll quote the leaders of this campaign. The queens made their move.

"I'm afraid we don't have much time. Our spells are getting weaker with every second. The portal will be opened again soon, and then even the Sculptor won't help us close it again. Our only chance is to try and break into the Architects' world and seal it from the inside.

I know this sounds very difficult. I believe in the Light's power, but I do realize that any power has its limits. I can't even imagine the place we are going to. Does it have the same physical laws? Will we even survive the journey? The Sculptor says, "our bodies should be functioning as usual". But let's put it this way: I'm not ready to trust such an odd creature.

Anyway, it's not like we have a choice. We will enter the portal together and put an end to this threat.  In the name of Light!"

So you're standing in front of that portal. The probability of a new invasion is significant... And you have already seen what happens when the Architects try to influence the living flesh of your world. Modificants, all this madness is what the Architects' influence brings.

You are lucky that the Sculptor has been separated from the Unity for so long. Or the Ascension and Transmutation would have been inevitable.

I'll quote the leaders of this campaign. The queens made their move.

"The portal will open again soon. I can feel strong magical disturbances around it. The time has come, and we can't wait anymore.

Frankly, I don't trust the Sculptor, and neither should you. His allegiance and motives are still unknown. He will help us enter the Architects' world, but he himself should remain here.

If what he says is true, then the first enemy we face will be the guard of the portal.  I don't think he will approve of our determination to destroy his precious Path. And we're going to be very thorough.

Let's do it!"

Do you believe the Sculptor? You'll have to trust his word.

So, do you want to know what will happen if you follow him to the Otherverse?

The battle with Locus was extremely difficult. But eventually he was defeated.

The harmony is gone... The Order is broken... Locus... Is no longer needed..." the Architect's voce said.

"To become perfect, you say?" Rysina said, crushing one of the Architect's cores. "Oops, I've stepped on your perfection! Hey, what's happening?"

"Locus is self-destructing! Run!" Marianne yelled.

"Move, move!" you all ran out of the center of the Order.

Locus fell apart...

"Oh... may the Light save us. Now that everything's over..." Marianne stopped to catch a breath.

"Nothing is over. Look around you!" As soon as you turned around, you saw a horde of Locuses that kept coming.

"Great Tensess..." Marianne managed to say.

Rysina was furious:

"Unbelievable... That thing! You tricked us! Lured us into a trap! We will destroy you! Destroy all of you, one after another!"

"Funny. If you destroy me, you will destroy your way home. I have fulfilled our agreement. You disrupted the Path, but you cannot defeat the Architect. Leave. Go back. Remember, children of chaos: the Order cannot be changed!" With those words, the Sculptor vanished.

When the expedition was over, the heroes received Zayan's letter.

"Good day!

First of all, let me congratulate you on surviving the battle with the Architects.

It is my duty to inform you that we have studied the cloning system and found answers to all our questions. You may find it interesting that this technology was initially developed on Ferris without the use of any otherworldly materials. The Object - or the Sculptor - provided the energy source for this miracle of engineering. That is why all clones, including pseudo-Herbert and pseudo-Elena, turned into modificants so quickly. Their high intelligence shows that the process of creating a living being from scratch went smoothly. However, the Sculptor's influence on the staff turned to be rather damaging.

Most likely, Tep had learned about the cloning technology and the principles of matter and energy manipulation during his visit to Ferris.

Sarn, the "Master" of the cultists, took high interest in the activities of Tep and his minions. This is how the cloning technology got into the hands of the cultist leader, Gorluxor. Comparing their cloning systems proves our theory true.

Well, this is it. Thank you for all your efforts in keeping our expedition safe. Murk is looking forward to another adventure like that one. He said, and I quote: "If you don't call me next time you fight these hunhurrs, you will regret it!"

Yours respectfully,

Zayan.

P.S.: Herbert and Elena have departed together to an unknown location. I know we probably won't see them in the League or the Empire again. Still, if you meet them again some day, tell them they are always welcome here."

This is how Marianne reacted:

"Well, so that happened. I could blame the Sculptor for his treachery, but what's the point? Obviously, we shouldn't have trusted him from the very beginning. He is too different from us.

I must admit I was hoping that, knowing what it's like to be completely alone, he wouldn't turn his back on us. But everyone makes mistakes, and I'm not an exception."

I suppose we are done here. Don't let the Sculptor's actions overshadow your triumph! You have accomplished a great feat. One of your greatest, probably.

I hope our victory puts an end to this story. I will hope and pray for this... Every day! Can the Architects return now that we have destroyed the Path? I'm afraid nobody knows that. So there is no point in worrying.

I have to decide what to do with the Historians and Ferris. The Empire's presence makes things more complicated. I don't think they are eager to share their secrets. However, I can handle this. You should go see Aidenus as soon as possible. He's the one who can tell us what to do."

This is how Aidenus summed it up:

"So that's how that happened. The Cataclysm taught us nothing! We continue to toy with forces that are beyond our understanding! First Nezeb with his vain efforts, and now Zayan with his endless search for knowledge... Ah, at least this time it ended well.

So... The Architects, uninvited guests from the beyond. As Tensess said, the universe only gives you what you can handle. This time these creatures met with a rebuff. If they come again, we will handle them one way or another. Would they dare to? We will keep an eye out for them! The Empire is not vain, so we'll crush them and be done with it!

I thank you for your great deed! You saved not only the League, but the entire Sarnaut. You cannot imagine how proud I am to have a hero like you in our ranks!"

You still don't understand what the Architects are? You've never faced anything like them before. Even demons, while devoid of all signs of individuality, are separate beings… But the creator of demons clearly thought about something like this when he tried to create his army. You are seeing perfect soldiers...

But only a witness of the events can tell you the whole story:

"First there was a Guard who wanted to drive us out of this world at any cost. Then there was a researcher who wanted to learn as much as possible about us... I'm still trying to figure out what the Architects want with us. What is their mission? And what's even more interesting - how do they think?

Look at the way they fight. No one of them stands idly by. They don't just help each other in battle - they complement each other. The attacks never cease. The defense is almost impeccable. When we advanced, they all reacted as one, regrouping and retreating. When we retreated, they pushed forward.

They don't have personal thoughts. They are all part of the same process and the same will." That's what the Sculptor said, and now I'm starting to see what he meant. And I sure don't like it..."

Colossus, the Armada Commander... A perfect tool. Created for one purpose. Now it's starting to make sense, no?

"So it's true. They can actually split into multiple different creatures... Or assemble into a monstrosity. What living being is capable of that? Come to think of it, how many Architects are there? We thought there were millions of them, but what... what if we've been fighting just one Architect this whole time?

It looks like we don't know what we're dealing with. If this is its normal state, is there a limit to its abilities?"

You still don't understand what the Architects are? You've never faced anything like them before. Even demons, while devoid of all signs of individuality, are separate beings… But the creator of demons clearly thought about something like this when he tried to create his army. You are seeing perfect soldiers...

But only a witness of the events can tell you the whole story:

"Can you feel it? Well, why would you - you're not as experienced in psionicism as I am. Even my expertise is not sufficient to fully comprehend the situation.

Well, I tried to read the minds of these creatures, and I could only hear the same thing. Their minds seem to be... connected somehow. They are not just acting as a whole. They think as a whole. And the more of them there are, the louder their thoughts are. What? What they are thinking about? Well, I will tell you later. It doesn't matter right now.

The point is, now the Architects' thoughts are so loud I can't get them out of my head! I feel the approach of something... colossal!"

Colossus, the Armada Commander... A perfect tool. Created for one purpose. Now it's starting to make sense, no?

"Well done! I've never seen you in action before. Now I see that the stories are true. But let's get back to the Architects.

Their peculiar way of thinking and their ability to change their bodies so easily suggests that there are no "Architects" - there is just one Architect. A single consciousness, distributed among many bodies that keep changing, fusing, and splitting? What if this is what the Sculptor meant? If so... well, that's very bad."

Your path takes you further... Through enemies that try to stop you. Isn't that the maxim of your life in Sarnaut?

But there's another milestone. Marianne de Ardeur:

"I have an odd feeling... Like darkness is gathering around us. Invisible, intangible. It's not even hostile. But it makes my skin crawl. Just look at this place - we have nowhere to go if we need to retreat. Everything here follows alien laws which we can't ever fathom. We don't have the time for scientific surveys. We just need to stay alive... Even Herbert wouldn't argue with that.

Very well... Let's cast all doubts aside! We must maintain our courage in the darkest of times. Otherwise, even our faith is useless. No Light can save weak-willed souls!

Come on! Let's find the source of this power and challenge it!"

Cascade, the Hive Commander...

A dangerous enemy! There's a reason his name makes you think of insects. The local residents will come swarming in to greet uninvited guests. It'll be difficult to keep moving.

"The darkness is gone. It's easier to breathe now... Can you feel it?

What a strange creature. At first, I sensed no aggression, but then... Well, it reminded me of Kanian children who cut off the tails of mice and set anthills on fire. Just to see what will happen. The creature was definitely studying us.

Whatever it was, it's gone. Let's move on."

Your path takes you further... Through enemies that try to stop you. Isn't that the maxim of your life in Sarnaut?

But there's another milestone. Ekaterina Rysina:

"I don't like this space. It looks huge, but it's still too small for a battle. And I also have a strange feeling that... Ah, never mind.

I think we need to climb that hill over there. We can't go anywhere else from here - the elven prioress is not great at opening portals, I'd say. Though I can't fault her for it - it's not what a prioress would normally be skilled at. Besides, our magic seems to be working unpredictably here, too.

Alright, let's not waste time. Move! Whoever stands in our way will regret it!"

Cascade, the Hive Commander...

A dangerous enemy! There's a reason his name makes you think of insects. The local residents will come swarming in to greet uninvited guests. It'll be difficult to keep moving.

"Well, I suspect the Architects will soon head this way, and they will be much stronger that the last two.

But I'm already starting to enjoy this. The more of them show up, the sooner we finish this."

The thing is, there are no Architects. There's only one Architect. One mind, one will.

He is his own god and priest, and the crowd that believes in him. He doesn't need anyone. He's whole. He embodies the Order in the way he understands it.

You're in the heart of the Otherverse now. Before you is Locus, the Creator.

Let's return to those who accompanied you on this journey.

"Light have mercy on us..." Marianne was at a loss for words.

"I don't think Light can help us here... What is that?" Even Rysina has never seen anything like it before.

This is Locus. Here matter acquires shape and becomes a part of the whole. Perfection is order. Order is integrity. If you disrupt Locus's integrity, you will disrupt the harmony of the world..." the Sculptor was unperturbed.

"This is not the time for philosophy! We have to stop him!" The head of the City Council was eager to fight.

"You? This is pointless. You cannot break such a perfect structure. Unless... You destroy matter! Destroy the Inferior! Then the existence of Locus will lose its meaning. We... I... The whole is calling me. Do not count on my help."

"We'll manage," said Rysina with disdain, but then you heard the Architect's voice:

"Children of chaos... Why did you come to my world? I am the Architect! I'm the Order! You are going to ascend. Become perfect. Become whole... Like our lost shard!"

The Sculptor gave you his last instructions:

"Your goal lies ahead of you. Do you still want to disrupt the Path? Reject the Ascension? Give in to the chaos that is devouring the worlds? So be it. I will help you reach Locus, the rest will be entirely up to you.

I will rearrange our world to let you reach Locus. I... The Architect will not like it. Parts of the Whole are already on their way here, so you will not reach your destination without a fight."

Marianne did not go with you:

"Oh, Light, I wish I could go with you, but I can't... Elizaveta and I are drained. All we can do is share with you the crumbs of whatever power we have left. I hope it will help you reach Locus and turn him to dust!

Frankly speaking, I'm not a big fan of landscapes, but... This world is beautiful in its own way.  It has its cold and magnetic charm... And this creature is extraordinary in its... rightness.

I don't feel well. I could use some rest, but here it's a luxury.  I'm afraid if I get closer to Locus, I... I'm sorry, but this time I can only help you with a blessing. This place is starting to affect me in a bad way...

Go! Fight, and remember - the fate of our world is in your hands. Elizaveta and I will come to the rescue if we feel that Locus is growing weaker. But until then, we will stay here and try to hold off the Architects. May the Light guide you!"

Rysina:

"Ah, demon spawn! I have a terrible headache...

The prioress and I are exhausted. I will send my mental messenger with you to carry the remains of my power. I hope it will help you. I can't do more - if I get any closer to Locus, he'll turn me into a drooling vegetable. This monster is way too strong!

So, Locus... That's new. I can feel him squeezing my head... My mind is foggy, and I can barely move. It looks like my weapon was turned against me... Not bad, not bad.

I'm too exhausted to continue fighting... If I can't trust myself, I'd better stay here and help you in other ways. The prioress won't be much use right now, either. She looks like she keeps it together, but there's nothing but prayers in her head. Well, at least now it's clear why the Sculptor didn't want to come here.

Now go and rip that monster apart! Its spawns are threatening our world, and that's why it has to die! Marianne and I will make sure nothing gets in your way!

Let's go!"

The Reaper, Guard of the Path.

You don't understand what creatures you're dealing with. Do they have needs, instincts, desires? Or are those constructs, automatons that have no will of their own? Understanding will come later.

You have only caught their attention so far. But don't expect them to focus on you, because such trespass occurs quite often. But they saw you, and there will be some kind of reaction.

I'll let those who were there with you speak:

"Oh... we barely made it. I knew it would be tough, but this thing turned out to be much stronger than I expected.

What will happen next?"

You have only caught their attention so far. But don't expect them to focus on you, because such trespass occurs quite often. But they saw you, and there will be some kind of reaction.

I'll let those who were there with you speak:

"That was... intense. We can't underestimate these creatures if we want to survive in here.

Keep your eyes open. It will only get worse."

So what do we have so far? One of the Aoidoi lost his lover and went a little crazy - he wants to destroy immortality. It's a tragic situation, but we can't let that happen. We need immortality.

Fortunately, Klavdia has a plan.

"Well, well, the boy is ambitious. He's barely an adult, but he's ready to go after an immortal being. They grow up so fast...!

Alright, let's be serious. The thing is, Kyros might actually be able to get it done. How do I know that? Does it matter? Well, let’s call it intuition. I can feel a mysterious power in him.

To follow Kyros into the portal, you will have to enter the Well of Souls. Yes, that pillar of light which spawns newborn Aoidoi. My magic will direct you to the Secret Paths, the deepest layer of the Planar Rim. I don't know what's waiting for you down there. If you are lucky, you will find an entrance to the Purgatory. You will be the first mortal in history to enter it alive. And you probably won't enjoy it...

But you're used to it, aren't you?"

There was one problem - the path to the Well was blocked by demons who had no intention of letting you through.

"I warned you... I warned you all! And yet, you are here.

I don't know what I expected! You're nothing but cowards, holding onto your so-called immortality. Well, then...

I'm glad you have something to fight for! It's a shame you will die for nothing!" Those were Kyros's words before he transformed and went to challenge the Servant of Tensess. You had no other choice but to follow him.

You made it to Purgatory before Kyros. The goblin innkeeper dropped his jaw when he saw you.

"What? I smell living flesh! What are you doing here?! You can't be here!"

And when you tried to warn him, he scoffed, "Kyros-shmyros! You can't just walk in here! It's Purgatory, not a market square!

There are no Kyroses in this place. I'd remember a name like that...

Wait. What's this noise?"

And the walls of Purgatory fell when Kyros made his way in. Gripping his scythe, he lunged at the Servant of Tensess.

Well, you won in the end. Kyros was defeated.

There are a lot of amazing creatures in this world, and you've never seen most of them. But the Secret Paths, and those who live here, are a different story. You were "lucky" to run into Simargl, the Guardian of Secret Paths.

This overgrown white six-legged cat loves riddles and games. She reminds me of one of our mutual acquaintances. However, games on the Secret Paths are very dangerous, and if you go the wrong way, you can be lost forever.

"Sweet sparks are coming to my Prism! They were lost on the Secret Paths... Poor things!

Will you play a game with me, sparks? If you win, I'll let you go. If I win, you will be wandering forever in my worlds. For I am the lock, and I am the key, and I make the rules on the Secret Paths!"

Fortunately, you managed to outwit this creature. Or else you'd be stuck somewhere on the Planar Rim.

The flow of time is frozen in this place. It seems that even the heart fell silent, following the rhythm of the Planar Rim. Its last beat was a century ago, and it'll be another century before the next one.

Your enemy is waiting in the middle of the Bridge of Times.

I think you remember the stranger you met with Kyros when you caught up with him on the island of the centaurs. As you understand, our friend Aoidos has not yet mastered the art of traveling across the Planar Rim. Someone carefully guided him to his goal, but who were they...?

Carefully look around before the battle begins - is there anything around that can help us?

Morrana will surround herself with loyal servants. It's best to hit them with her own magic. But be careful - too much ancient magic can play a cruel trick on you."

Fortunately, even the Scroll of Tensess didn't help this witch.

"She's not the first one to fall because of her own arrogance. And not the last one. Whether fortunately or unfortunately, only time will show.

We're halfway through. The way to the inner chamber is open now. Keep your guard up: even I don't know what dangers lie ahead. Greatest warriors and most skillful mages are buried in these tombs. The Demon will surely summon them to its aid! On the other hand, not every creature it summons will obey it..."

The masks are discarded. The ghost turned out to be Reniesta, that “number 4 from Umoir”. The traitor whose name was forever tainted. The Demon and those he controlled were waiting ahead. I guess I'll let her speak:

"What's with the scroll and the cape, you ask? Tensess himself gave them to Skrakan. Why? For what purpose? I don’t know for sure. I suppose Tensess wanted to protect Skrakan during his experiment. But the Great Mage summoned an ancient demon to Umoir by mistake, and everything went pear-shaped. Animals turned into monsters, spirits went crazy... The Blight started then, do you understand? My friends stopped it. They defeated the demon and laid it to rest for all eternity.

At least that's what I thought... But then this stupid girl Catherina brought the damned thing back to life. And the whole thing started all over again. What's even worse, my friends, is that Danas, Fergard, and Naira were buried here together with their bitter enemy. The people of Umoir believed that this was the way to protect the dead from the corruption of demonic magic. That was a grievous mistake. Now the three of them will forever be the Demon's slaves.

I beg you to end their suffering. And be careful! They are experienced warriors, and it won't be easy to defeat them. Besides, the Demon has surely granted them a piece of his foul power. The scroll and the cape will help you in this battle. Use the scroll to break the connection between the heroes and the Demon. The cape will protect you from the deadliest attacks and spells.

Good luck! I will be praying for you... There's nothing else for me to do.

There was a glorious hero with us, Sir Brian. He was a paladin. His sword ended my life when I deceived my friends. His sword brought me back to life. Ancient magic works in mysterious ways..."

You were standing on the ancient burial ground, feeling the cold of the dungeons. Before you were the old heroes of Sarnaut, now slaves to a ruthless demon.

"Here they come, the heroes of Sarnaut! Blind fools coming to meet their death!" said Fergard.

"This scum dares to challenge Sarn? Challenge us?!" exclaimed Danas in outrage.

"They want to lay with us in the dark tombs of the Burial Mound? How can we deny them?" said Naira snidely.

And a terrible battle began - with those who had once been the defenders of Sarnaut. They had already defeated the Demon, but now they fought on its side.

As soon as you defeated them, it appeared from its grave:

"Your victories mean nothing, and you are nothing. Servants of Shadow who call themselves warriors of Light! Keep holding onto your trinkets! They did not help these fools. Raise, you slaves! You are doomed to fight... forever!"

"We... obey. We are one!" Those were the words of the fallen heroes.

But even the Demon was unable to fight off your onslaught.

"Well... So be it. Enjoy your victory while you can. Live in your bloody world! I have eternity!" Sarn's Demon disappeared after that.

Ancient bird maidens. Once upon a time, there were many of them, but alas, all good things disappear with time. There are just a few of them left. It's fortunate that some of them are on Umoir... But is it really? One of them has fallen under the influence of the Blight...

It's sad. There is not enough beauty in this world...

I'll let our guide speak:

We are close to the center of the Mound, the Heroes' tombs. One last guard stands in our way...

Have you heard about the bird of sorrow, Sirin? Two mystical birds lived here, on Umoir. Sirin and Gamayun. They spent centuries in this place, and saw both glorious and dark days. Gamayun sang songs of happiness and joy, while Sirin sang about sweet sorrow and hard lessons taught by the past.

As time went by, there was more sorrow than joy. I couldn't understand what made Sirin hide in these catacombs, but then it hit me! It was Catherina who imprisoned her in this gloomy place. Sirin was meant to sing about all the evil deeds of the queen, and to predict the end of Umoir. Who would possibly enjoy listening to this?

Unfortunately, Sirin stayed here for too long. The Demon's influence corrupted her body and mind. Now her songs are full of poison, and all she sings about is pain and death. We must end her suffering.

The problem is, she could use this area to her advantage. If she manages to fly high, it will be hard to defeat her - she can easily kill you all from up there. Try using her poisonous slime on her...

All birds keep their feathers clean. If you smear them with her own slime, she will be distracted and won't fly up. She will furiously beat her wings, and that's when you must strike."

Well, Sirin was defeated. And her death led to some revelations from your ghostly helper:

Sirin was singing songs of sorrow and despair, peering into souls and digging up secrets. I can't do this anymore! I have a confession to make. There's something I've been hiding from you.

My name is Reniesta. I first came to Umoir with my sworn sister and brothers a long time ago. We were trying to find out what happened to the Great Mage Skrakan. We saw a lot. We walked along many roads together. We fought shoulder to shoulder...

After everything we'd been through, I betrayed them. Betrayed my friends, my allies! For what? For some scroll and cape!"

This place attracts all kinds of vermin. The giant toad, ancient undead... And you haven't even reached the entrance yet! You want to know what happened next?

So, next enemy. That's what someone else said about it:

"Now it's time to face the most dreadful Blighted creature you can find on Umoir. To tell you the truth, it's not just the Blight that created it. It's a real magical conundrum.

Eye Stare is one of the oldest Treants in this place. Long ago it started dabbling in death magic, and its brethren exiled it to the Burial Mound. Which worked in its favor, because this place was exactly where it wanted to be. Plenty of dead bodies to raise, plenty of restless souls to let into its body. After a while, it lost its mind and decided it was the king of the local undead. When the Blight came, it readily accepted it, too. It became a loyal servant of the Demon. The locals were calling it Asura One Eye. Which doesn't tell you how terrifying it is. You'll see.

What really troubles me is its ability to turn invisible and attack from behind. It may invade your minds, so stay alert. Try using ashes from the urns here to reveal it when it's hidden, but be fast! The longer it stays disguised, the stronger it becomes.

Of course, Eye Stare also got itself some minions! It summoned the dead, and they answered its call. They can also become invisible, but luckily, ashes reveal them, too.

Do you understand now? This is where evil forces have been gathering.

It's a good thing you dealt with Eye Stare... You even got an interesting trophy.

"That's how Eye Stare keeps itself hidden! It had an ancient relic on it, a magical cape which I've seen before. Destiny's sense of humor is... peculiar.

Here's another joke. While you were fighting Eye Stare, guess who entered the Mound? Morrana herself. With the Scroll of Tensess in her hands! But first things first."

Interesting. The Blight is an incredible phenomenon. It's basically Life in a different form. It's too bad we can't coexist with it.

But there's a power that always opposes Life: Death. It's a good thing when your enemies help you defeat them. You don't understand?

Alright, let me tell you what that sorceress said:

"The monster maned Zomgie can raise the dead from their graves. It will be extremely difficult to defeat it since there's a huge cemetery around us. Thankfully, Blighted carnivorous plants don't like the living dead, so nature is going to be your ally in this fight against Death. It will distract the undead horde while you are fighting Zomgie.

So if you go through the Burial Grounds, you'll have to deal with Zomgie. Watch where it's looking. Its stare can be deadly."

The Winter Palace... It's an interesting place. Built in the style of the Elven royalty. Alas, it has seen better days.

I'll repeat Eladia's words:

"This king of the Free Traders has built quite a palace! It's more of a museum, actually.

Did you know Ivan Chelezny is an esteemed collector? He gets his hands on all sorts of pieces of art, from silicon axes to elven statues, and the biggest part of his collection is stored in his country residence. I guess the old man spends his time looking at all his ill-gotten gains.

I hear there's so much gold in his treasury that the chests are overflowing with it. It's nice being a Free Trader, huh. The place is now occupied by the fanatics, so the museum is slowly turning into either a brothel or a nuthouse."

Well, if you hurry, you might save more than a few genuine artworks.

Eladia also said,

"Personally I think there are too many gods, demigods, and other mythic figures in our world. We need to reduce their ranks. Let's start with that big-mouthed goblin who calls himself the Prophet, and the dumb minotaur who called me... eh, never mind.

Any objections? No? That's what I thought!

Come on, gather your allies, and let's go!"

The war is over, but we still need to deal with the consequences, right? At least only Dane was affected.

And what do we have here? More cultists, only this time they worship Order? A strange goblin prophesying a new order?

Let me tell you what others have said:

"I knew there was someone more powerful behind the fanatics and the Prophet. At first I thought it could be a Great Mage, but when I heard them mention the Sculptor - and nobody told me about him for some reason! - everything became clear. However, I can only speculate about the purpose of their experiments. And my speculations are not comforting at all.

As you can remember, faith is a great power which can literally move mountains. The Architects - or should I say the Architect - is using the power of self-assertion. He believes in himself, and he is unflinching in his faith in the special purpose of his mind. But the Sculptor has lost that power when he detached himself from the whole. Now he is trying to compensate by creating monsters who look like him and have infinite faith in his power.

You see what the problem is? If the Sculptor succeeds in creating a sentient chimera using human and Architect flesh, and that creature will be a believer, we will face a catastrophe comparable in scale to the invasion of Dane! This is what the Prophet and the fanatics want - to create an army of chimeras who know no doubt or hesitation and believe in the divinity of the Sculptor."

We need to prevent that before it turns into a global problem... You want to hear the story?

So the Cult of Order fell apart soon after it was formed. The Sculptor disappeared without a trace.

It looked like the war was over. The Architects' invasion was rebuffed, the Sculptor's schemes were foiled, but the threat of another attack loomed. For the Architects, failure in one of the worlds was just a delay of the inevitable. And then there was also Sarn. The mad god hasn't stopped trying to free himself, and every attempt put this world on the brink of destruction. And somewhere beyond the borders of this world, Nihaz was thirsting for revenge, his eyes glued to whatever was happening in Sarnaut.

There were also people willing to risk everything to save this world. Instead of waiting for the next cataclysm, they acted...

Finally, the last battle.

The battle for the Winter Palace ended with the battle against Bedlam - that very chimera which consisted of different parts and used the power of faith. Fortunately, this threat was dealt with before it became a crisis. However, you never met the Sculptor himself - he mysteriously disappeared.

"Oh my... Living statues in the yard - and a stone demigod on the roof! I must admit, I wasn’t expecting that. Now I'm even more eager to meet the Sculptor, but our friend is cautious... I’m sure we'll meet one day, and then I'll beat the living daylights out of him. But the threat was averted - the fanatics scattered, and the bandits surrendered to the authorities!"

Goblins. They are everywhere. They can be quite useful, but they cause a lot of harm.

You want to know about that Prophet, the self-proclaimed religious activist?

These are Eladia's words:

"The Prophet... I wonder where that crazy goblin came from. And how can people be such idiots?

Who in their right mind can believe a goblin on stilts wearing a colorful robe and carrying a dead Architect core under his arm? This is pure madness. Maybe that's his secret? If one combines pure madness with infinite faith, it can become a terrifying weapon in the hands of a skillful puppet master, and the Sculptor is a brilliant manipulator.

By the way, I heard there was a fire in a hospice right after the first Architects' attack on the Iron City. It was burned to the ground along with its patients and the staff which usually consists of goblins. Some of the bodies were not found. Maybe this twisted faith in the "holy Architects" was born in that fire?"

You mean Ivan's assistant? That Hoof? The traitor who tried to kill you? Greed has ruined so many lives.

This is what Eladia thinks about it:

"What about Hoof? He's just a greedy boor who will sell his own mother for a handful of gold. But now this animal wears an Assault Shell and carries a Meteorite hammer that can crush walls. Still, I don't think he'll be a problem for you. He's not Tep after all, and definitely not my father... But that rage of gold and blood can consume a being to the point where they feel nothing but blind fury whenever anyone tries to take their treasure from them. He will fight for his gold to the last drop of blood, that's for sure.

 If you defeat the Prophet and Hoof, the rest of the bandits and fanatics will scatter. There'll be no one standing between us and the Sculptor."

Statues of elven heroes? You don't need to hear their stories for now...

Eladia will tell you the rest:

"You mean those in the park?  I don't like them either. It's so weird to see elves without wings!

I read about those statues in a popular science magazine, "Science & Death", in the Supernatural section. The Historians discovered elven ruins on a distant allod which dates back to ancient times. The destroyed city was built by the Elves before the Change - which means long before the Cataclysm.

Just imagine how excited the archeologists were - the five elven statues remained intact among the ruins and ash! Too bad the ancient elves didn't like uninvited guests, so the second expedition found only withered remains of the first one at the feet of the statues. The second expedition was found dead on an Astral ship which was looted by pirates... The pirate ship was later discovered on a shore on Suslanger, and the statues turned up on the black market some time later. Eventually, an anonymous collector bought them.

Some say the statues are cursed, some say they contain ancient elven magic or even the Sparks of heroes of the past... It seems you'll be the one to uncover the truth."
